engagement_name: Customer Churn Reduction Platform — NorthStar Telecom
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0301

Client: NorthStar Telecom BV (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: Insights & Data
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 18 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will design, build and operationalise a machine-learning-powered Customer Churn Prediction and Intervention Platform for NorthStar Telecom's residential broadband division. The platform will ingest real-time usage telemetry, CRM event data and customer service interaction logs to produce daily propensity-to-churn scores at the individual customer level. A next-best-action recommendation engine will surface targeted retention offers to the contact centre and digital self-service channels within 24 hours of a risk threshold being breached.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
The engagement is structured around three primary outcome KPIs, each with a confirmed baseline:
  (a) Voluntary churn rate: reduce from approximately 2.8% per month to ≤2.0% per month across the residential broadband base, measured on a rolling 90-day average by end of Month 12 post-go-live.
  (b) Retention offer acceptance rate: achieve ≥34% acceptance on AI-surfaced retention interventions, versus a current baseline of around 19% on manually selected offers.
  (c) Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) uplift: deliver a material incremental CLV improvement across the intervention cohort within 18 months, verified using a randomised holdout group.
Baseline data has been validated and a measurement methodology, including holdout group design and attribution rules, will be agreed at contract execution.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Fees are structured as a fixed build component covering Months 1–6 (platform design, model development, integration, UAT), and an at-risk performance component payable in tranches at Month 12 and Month 18, contingent on achievement of outcome KPIs (a) and (c). Partial payment applies for near-target achievement. A shared gain clause applies if churn reduction materially exceeds the target.

4. GOVERNANCE AND MEASUREMENT
A joint Outcome Review Board will convene monthly, co-chaired by Contoso Consulting's Engagement Director and NorthStar's Chief Customer Officer. Outcome measurement will use NorthStar's existing data infrastructure; Contoso Consulting will not have write access to production systems.

engagement_name: Finance Shared Services Transformation — Meridian Pharma Group
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0302

Client: Meridian Pharma Group plc (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: Business Services
Contract Type: Time & Materials
Engagement Duration: 24 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will provide finance transformation consultants and technology specialists to support Meridian Pharma Group's global Finance Shared Services Centre (FSSC) migration programme. The engagement covers process redesign for Order-to-Cash, Purchase-to-Pay and Record-to-Report towers across multiple European entities. Contoso Consulting resources will be embedded within the client programme management office. The scope explicitly excludes any post-go-live operational responsibility.

2. DELIVERABLES
Deliverables are defined as process maps (current and future state), system configuration documents, data migration scripts, test scripts, and training materials. Acceptance criteria are technical: client sign-off on each deliverable within 10 business days of submission. There are no post-implementation performance targets defined in the SoW, and no KPIs linked to business outcomes such as days sales outstanding (DSO), cost per transaction or error rates. Meridian's Group CFO has indicated that outcome-linked payment terms will not be accepted under current procurement policy.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
All Contoso Consulting resources will be billed at agreed day rates per grade. Travel and expenses are reimbursed at cost. The contract includes a rolling termination clause on either side.

4. CONSTRAINTS
The client's procurement policy currently restricts contingent fee or risk-sharing arrangements with third-party technology vendors. Contoso Consulting's commercial team has noted this constraint and confirmed it renders outcome-based pricing structurally infeasible for this engagement at this time.

STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0303

Client: Vanguard Insurance NV (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: Financial Services
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 12 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will redesign and automate Vanguard Insurance's end-to-end motor claims intake and triage process. The solution combines intelligent document processing (IDP), a rules-based triage engine for straight-through processing (STP), and an AI-assisted damage assessment module integrated with Vanguard's existing claims management platform. Human-in-the-loop review will be retained for higher-complexity claims.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
Outcome KPIs with confirmed baselines:
  (a) Straight-through processing rate: increase from around 31% to ≥55% of eligible motor claims by end of Month 10.
  (b) Average claims cycle time: reduce from approximately 11 days to ≤6 days for STP-eligible claims, measured as FNOL receipt to settlement authorisation.
  (c) Customer satisfaction (CSAT) on claims journey: achieve ≥4.1/5.0 on the post-settlement survey (current baseline around 3.6/5.0).
Note: The survey question weighting for the digital channel has not yet been finalised. This represents a minor gap that Contoso Consulting proposes to resolve during the Discovery phase.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
A fixed fee covers the platform build phase. An at-risk performance component is payable at engagement end contingent on achieving KPIs (a) and (b). KPI (c) acts as a satisfaction threshold; failure to meet it triggers a service credit. Commercial structure has been approved in principle; final sign-off is at board level.

4. GOVERNANCE
Monthly outcome review calls between Contoso Consulting Delivery Lead and Vanguard's Head of Claims Operations. Quarterly steering committee with CFO attendance. All outcome measurements will be conducted by Vanguard's independent analytics team.

engagement_name: Digital Twin Factory Operations — Heidel Manufacturing
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0304

Client: Heidel Manufacturing GmbH (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: Digital Manufacturing
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 24 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will develop and deploy a Digital Twin solution for Heidel Manufacturing's flagship production facility, covering multiple CNC machining lines and assembly cells. The Digital Twin will integrate real-time sensor data from IoT endpoints into a model layer, with a live visualisation and anomaly detection dashboard accessible to shift supervisors and central engineering. A predictive maintenance module will generate work orders in the ERP system automatically when degradation thresholds are breached.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
  (a) Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE): improve from a confirmed baseline of approximately 71% to ≥82% across the CNC lines within 18 months of go-live. OEE is measured weekly using Heidel's existing MES data.
  (b) Unplanned downtime incidents: reduce materially from current baseline by Month 18, measured from ERP work order data.
  (c) Scrap and rework cost: achieve a meaningful percentage reduction in monthly scrap cost by Month 18, verified by Heidel's finance controller.
  (d) Maintenance cost per machine: reduce to a target agreed at contract execution by the end of the 24-month period.
All baselines have been validated. A measurement protocol has been agreed. Heidel's engineering team has committed a dedicated data integration resource.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Phase 1 covers build and integration (fixed fee). Phase 2 includes an annual performance component structured as quarterly payments calculated against OEE and downtime KPI achievement. A stretch bonus applies if OEE materially exceeds the target. The commercial model has been approved by Heidel's Board of Directors.

4. DATA AND INTEGRATION
Heide will provide API access to MES and ERP systems. Contoso Consulting will deploy edge compute nodes on-premises; all data remains within Heidel's sovereign cloud boundary.

engagement_name: Workforce Analytics Platform — Albrecht Retail Group
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0305

Client: Albrecht Retail Group SE (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: People & Organisation
Contract Type: Time & Materials
Engagement Duration: 12 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will deliver a Workforce Analytics platform for Albrecht Retail Group's HR function, covering a large employee base across multiple European markets. The platform will integrate data from the client's HCM system, payroll and regional time-tracking tools to produce dashboards on headcount, attrition, absenteeism and workforce cost. The engagement also includes a capability-building programme for HR business partners.

2. OUTCOMES AND MEASUREMENT
The SoW references desired outcomes including 'improve workforce visibility', 'reduce time to insight for HR decisions' and 'support strategic workforce planning'. No baseline measurements have been provided. The client has indicated that baseline data collection is planned but will not be available until after the platform is expected to be live. Specific KPI targets were discussed in discovery but were not included in the final SoW because 'the business is not yet ready to commit to specific numbers'. No measurement methodology or holdout design has been agreed.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Contoso Consulting will be remunerated on a T&M basis. There are no performance-linked fees, milestone bonuses or outcome clauses in the current commercial structure. The client declined to include an outcome-linked element at this stage.

4. NOTE
This engagement has been noted as a candidate for outcome-based repricing at the next contract renewal, contingent on the client agreeing to baseline measurement during the initial platform deployment phase.

engagement_name: Supply Chain Control Tower — Fortuna Consumer Goods
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0306

Client: Fortuna Consumer Goods NV (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: Supply Chain & Operations
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 15 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will implement an end-to-end Supply Chain Control Tower for Fortuna Consumer Goods across its Western European distribution network. The Control Tower will integrate demand sensing signals, supplier lead-time feeds, logistics track-and-trace data and inventory positions into a unified operational view. AI-driven exception management will surface supply risk events earlier than Fortuna's current process, enabling proactive intervention.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
  (a) Perfect Order Rate: improve from a baseline of approximately 87% to ≥93% within 12 months of go-live, measured monthly.
  (b) Inventory holding cost reduction: achieve a meaningful reduction in average inventory days-on-hand across distribution centres by Month 12.
  (c) Supply disruption response time: reduce mean time from disruption detection to corrective action materially, measured from event log data.
  (d) Logistics cost per case: reduce to a target agreed at contract execution by Month 15, verified by Fortuna's finance team.
All baselines confirmed from Fortuna's ERP and logistics systems. Independent measurement by Fortuna's Group Supply Chain Analytics team.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Fixed platform build fee for Months 1–6. At-risk performance component payable at Month 12 and Month 15 based on achievement of KPIs (a), (b) and (d). KPI (c) is a service level threshold — missing it for two consecutive months triggers a service credit. An additional stretch bonus applies if Perfect Order Rate materially exceeds target. Board-level approval received.

4. DEPENDENCIES
Fortuna will provide a dedicated integration team for ERP connectivity. A data governance framework for supplier data sharing is being finalised.

engagement_name: Cloud Infrastructure Managed Services — Berova Financial Services
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0307

Client: Berova Financial Services Ltd (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: Cloud Infrastructure & Security
Contract Type: Fixed Retainer (Managed Services)
Engagement Duration: 36 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will provide managed services for Berova Financial Services' Azure cloud estate, covering virtual machines, Kubernetes clusters, database tiers and associated networking. Services include 24/7 monitoring, incident management, patching, capacity management and monthly architecture review.

2. SERVICE LEVELS AND MEASUREMENT
SLAs are defined for platform availability, incident response times and change success rate. Penalty credits apply for availability shortfalls. No business outcome KPIs are included in the contract. Berova's CTO confirmed that the bank's risk and procurement policies restrict outcome-based pricing for infrastructure managed services, as infrastructure uptime is not considered a directly attributable revenue driver.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Monthly fixed retainer covering all in-scope services up to a defined volume threshold. Consumption above the threshold is billed at an agreed per-unit rate. Annual price indexation applies. Contoso Consulting's proposal to include an outcome-linked component (e.g. cloud cost optimisation savings share) was declined by the client.

4. REGULATORY CONTEXT
Berova is regulated under applicable financial services frameworks. These regulations require that service levels be defined in absolute, measurable terms. Outcome-based pricing was assessed as creating regulatory ambiguity and was excluded on that basis.

STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0308

Client: Castellan Energy plc (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: Procurement & Supply Chain
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 18 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will deliver an AI-Powered Procurement Optimisation programme for Castellan Energy covering the company's indirect spend categories (IT, facilities, professional services, logistics). The programme includes spend analytics, supplier rationalisation, AI-assisted sourcing event management, contract compliance monitoring and a supplier performance management framework. Contoso Consulting will work alongside Castellan's procurement team, not replace it.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
All targets agreed with Castellan's Group CPO and CFO, with baselines drawn from the prior fiscal year:
  (a) Addressable spend savings: deliver verified, recurring annual savings across in-scope categories by a defined month. Savings will be validated by Castellan's finance team using a standard savings methodology agreed at contract execution.
  (b) Supplier base rationalisation: reduce active suppliers in scope to a target number by Month 12, with high spend consolidation to preferred suppliers.
  (c) Contract compliance rate: improve purchase-order-backed spend materially by Month 15, measured from procurement system data.
  (d) Sourcing cycle time: reduce average competitive tender cycle significantly by Month 12.
Savings validation methodology is agreed. Baselines are confirmed from procurement and finance systems.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Contoso Consulting's fee includes a retained advisory component for the diagnostic and strategy phase, followed by a success-based component linked to verified savings delivered above a defined floor. The success component is capped over the engagement term. This structure aligns Contoso Consulting's economic incentive with Castellan's procurement value realisation. Approved by Castellan's Executive Committee.

4. GOVERNANCE
A Savings Governance Board co-chaired by Contoso Consulting's Programme Director and Castellan's CPO will meet monthly. All savings claims require sign-off from Castellan Finance and a named category manager before being counted against the success fee threshold.

engagement_name: SAP S/4HANA Greenfield Rollout — Delvaux Industrial Group
sow_text:
STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0309

Client: Delvaux Industrial Group SA (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: Enterprise Applications
Contract Type: Fixed Price
Engagement Duration: 30 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will lead the full lifecycle delivery of a SAP S/4HANA greenfield implementation for Delvaux Industrial Group, replacing legacy ERP systems across multiple legal entities. The programme covers Finance, Procurement, Manufacturing, Sales and Group Reporting.

2. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA AND DELIVERABLES
The contract defines acceptance criteria that are entirely technical and functional in nature: system performance benchmarks, data migration accuracy, functional test pass rate, and user training completion rate. No business outcome KPIs are included in the SoW. Measurable post-go-live business outcomes were proposed by Contoso Consulting during the sales cycle but were rejected by Delvaux's procurement team: the SAP programme is treated primarily as a compliance and infrastructure upgrade, and business outcomes are considered dependent on post-programme change management activities outside of Contoso Consulting's scope.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Fixed-price contract payable against defined project milestones. A retention is held until post go-live acceptance. Contoso Consulting carries delivery risk under the fixed-price model. A change control process governs scope changes. No outcome-linked fees, gain-share or performance bonuses are included or permitted under the current commercial terms.

4. CONSTRAINTS
The programme operates under applicable data privacy and security regulations. Introducing outcome-based pricing into this contract would require a full renegotiation of the fixed-price terms and approval from Delvaux's supervisory board.

STATEMENT OF WORK — Engagement Reference OPP-2026-0310

Client: Solaris Bank AG (fictional)
Contoso Consulting Practice: Customer Experience & Digital
Contract Type: Outcome-Based (proposed)
Engagement Duration: 12 months

1. SCOPE OF WORK
Contoso Consulting will redesign and digitise the end-to-end onboarding journey for Solaris Bank's SME banking product, covering business current account opening, KYC/AML document collection and initial credit assessment. The redesigned journey will replace a multi-step paper-assisted process with a fully digital self-service flow, supported by automated document verification, open banking data ingestion for financial health assessment, and an AI-assisted credit decisioning model.

2. MEASURABLE OUTCOMES AND SUCCESS CRITERIA
Baselines confirmed from Solaris Bank's recent operational data:
  (a) Time-to-account-open: reduce materially from current baseline for the majority of SME applications by Month 9.
  (b) Onboarding abandonment rate: reduce significantly from current baseline by Month 9.
  (c) KYC straight-through rate: increase meaningfully from current baseline of submitted KYC packs requiring no manual intervention.
  (d) Net Promoter Score (NPS) for onboarding journey: improve substantially from current baseline, measured via in-app survey with statistical significance confirmed.
Note: KPI (d) has a sample size dependency. Contoso Consulting has flagged this as a measurement risk and proposed a fallback metric (CSAT) if NPS sample remains below threshold.

3. COMMERCIAL MODEL
Discovery and design phase: fixed fee. Build and test phase: fixed fee. Performance period: outcome-based fee tied to KPIs (a), (b) and (c) with a defined weighting. KPI (d) acts as a satisfaction guardrail; failure triggers a service credit. Total contract value up to a defined maximum. Approved by Solaris Bank's COO and CFO.

4. REGULATORY AND COMPLIANCE
All AI models used in credit decisioning will comply with applicable AI regulation requirements. An AI model card and explainability report will be produced. Contoso Consulting's AI Ethics team will conduct a bias assessment prior to go-live.
